title.ja: こんにちは！毎日のあいさつ

description.vi: Những câu chào hỏi, giới thiệu bản thân và cảm ơn đơn giản nhất trong tiếng Việt.
description.en: The simplest Vietnamese phrases for greeting people, introducing yourself and saying thank you.
description.ja: あいさつ、自己紹介、お礼など、ベトナム語のいちばん基本的な表現です。

note.en: Vietnamese greets with chào + a kinship pronoun. The younger speaker calls herself em and calls an older woman chị; the final ạ adds respect.
note.ja: ベトナム語では「chào＋人称代名詞」であいさつします。年下の人は自分を em、年上の女性を chị と呼びます。文末の ạ は丁寧さを表します。

sentences.text: Chào anh, anh có khỏe không?

translations.ja: こんにちは、お元気ですか？

note.en: Pronouns are reciprocal: an older man is called anh ("you") and also calls himself anh ("I"), while he calls the younger person em.
note.ja: 人称は相互的です。年上の男性は相手から anh（あなた）と呼ばれ、自分のことも anh（私）と言い、年下の相手を em と呼びます。

note.en: Tone check: cũng has the ngã tone (~, rising with a catch in the throat) and khỏe has the hỏi tone (hook, low dipping). Northern speakers keep them distinct; in the South they sound alike.
note.ja: 声調に注意：cũng は ngã 声調（~、喉を締めて上がる）、khỏe は hỏi 声調（フック、低く下がる）。北部では区別しますが、南部ではほぼ同じに聞こえます。

note.en: Tôi is the neutral, polite "I" — safe with strangers and in formal situations when you don't know the other person's age.
note.ja: Tôi は中立的で丁寧な「私」です。初対面の人や、相手の年齢がわからない改まった場面で使えます。

note.en: Bạn literally means "friend". It is a friendly "you" for people around your own age, and common among young people and in classrooms.
note.ja: Bạn は本来「友達」という意味で、同年代の相手への親しみのある「あなた」です。若い人同士や教室でよく使われます。

translations.ja: お会いできてうれしいです。
さようなら、また会いましょう！
